gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each under-$500 1 kWh unit ships with and accepts: Anker's own page lists the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 as "Expandable Capacity: No", with only an AC cable in the box, a two-step solar window (11-28 V at 8.2 A, 29-60 V at 14.5 A) and 4-9 week shipping, while BLUETTI boxes a car cable but no solar cable with the Elite 100 mini.
standout_why: Compared against PopSci (cited), willitrunpower, outagepowerguide and powersized, all opened 2026-11-27. PopSci already says the BP1000 battery fits the original C1000 only and not the Gen 2, and willitrunpower already says the original C1000 is the only ~1 kWh unit under $500 that takes a real expansion battery, so the expansion half is not new. None of the four gives a solar connector, a solar voltage or amp window, or which charging cables are in the box, and willitrunpower's Gen 2 ship note ("early December", dated Nov 19) is older than Anker's current 4-9 week notice. The piece that would have scored higher, DJI's proprietary SDC solar and car accessories for the Power 1000 V2, I could not open on any DJI US page.
decides: It takes the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 out of contention for the pick: Anker's page says all orders ship within 4-9 weeks, which is past the page's four-week rule, and the unit cannot be expanded later. It leaves the rest of the ranking where it was. No under-$500 1 kWh unit I could read on a maker page takes an extra battery; EcoFlow's store names extra batteries on the $579 DELTA 3, not on the $459 DELTA 3 Classic listing. For our rows, the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini honestly wins the car-charging segment out of the box (car cable included, Charger 1 pairing named by BLUETTI), but solar needs a cable or bundle bought separately. The DJI Power 1000 V2 pick stays unverified on this angle.

findings.label: Expansion battery
findings.value: Not supported: spec table reads "Expandable Capacity: No"; FAQ says the unit "does not include an expansion feature"

findings.note: Maker's US product page. The page does not name the BP1000; PopSci's 11-26 roundup separately says the BP1000 fits the original C1000 only.

findings.label: Solar input window
findings.value: 600 W max, 60 V max; MPPT 11-28 V at 8.2 A, 29-60 V at 14.5 A
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US store)
findings.note: Our arithmetic from Anker's figures: below 29 V the input tops out at 28 V × 8.2 A = about 230 W; reaching 600 W needs about 41.4 V or more (600 ÷ 14.5), so panels wired in series under the 60 V ceiling. The page text gives no connector type.
